Cache Lab

Cache Control Override via Workers

Force a 3600 second CDN edge TTL whenever the origin responds with a Cache-Control: max-age=x header — using the Workers Cache API, because the cf.cacheTtl option can’t be set after you’ve read the response.

The problem Flow Six steps Worker code Header anatomy API details Decision tree CF-Cache-Status Live check Limitations Deploy

The core problem

Why not just use fetch() with cf options?

Cloudflare’s cf.cacheTtl option must be set before the fetch() call is made. But the origin’s Cache-Control header is only readable after the response arrives — and you can’t retroactively change the cache instruction on a request that already went out.

The bind: you need to read the response header to decide the TTL, but the cf object must be provided before you can read that header. With a single fetch() those two requirements are mutually exclusive — so we use the Cache API to store the response ourselves, after inspecting it.

Request flow

What the Worker does on every incoming request.

🌐
Request arrives
GET / HEAD
📂
Check cache
cache.match()
📦
Fetch origin
no cf override
🔍
Inspect headers
read max-age
💾
Store & respond
cache.put()

How the Worker operates

Six logical steps executed on every request.

1

Skip non-cacheable methods

Only GET and HEAD are cacheable by spec. Anything else (POST, PUT…) is forwarded straight to the origin.

2

Check the cache first

cache.match(cacheKey) looks up the URL in this data center’s cache. A HIT returns immediately — the origin is never contacted.

3

Fetch origin (no cf override)

On a MISS, a plain fetch(request) hits the origin. No cf options, because we don’t yet know the origin’s max-age.

4

Skip errors

If the origin returns non-2xx (!originResponse.ok), pass it through unchanged — never cache 4xx/5xx and poison the cache.

5

Parse max-age

A regex /\bmax-age=(\d+)\b/ reads the origin Cache-Control. Present → override; absent → pass through unmodified.

6

Override CDN TTL & store

Clone the response, rewrite Cache-Control to s-maxage=3600 (CDN TTL) while keeping the original max-age (browser TTL), then cache.put() via ctx.waitUntil().

Complete Worker code

Plain JavaScript — drop it into your worker.js.

copied 
export default {
  async fetch(request, env, ctx) {

    // Step 1 — Skip non-cacheable HTTP methods
    if (!["GET", "HEAD"].includes(request.method)) {
      return fetch(request);
    }

    const CLOUDFLARE_CDN_TTL = 3600; // 1 hour
    const cache    = caches.default;
    const cacheKey = new Request(request.url, request);

    // Step 2 — Return cached response if available (cache HIT)
    const cachedResponse = await cache.match(cacheKey);
    if (cachedResponse) {
      return cachedResponse;
    }

    // Step 3 — Cache MISS: fetch from origin without cf overrides
    const originResponse = await fetch(request);

    // Step 4 — Do not cache error responses
    if (!originResponse.ok) {
      return originResponse;
    }

    // Step 5 — Read and parse the origin's Cache-Control header
    const originCacheControl = originResponse.headers.get("Cache-Control") ?? "";
    const maxAgeMatch       = originCacheControl.match(/\bmax-age=(\d+)\b/);

    if (maxAgeMatch) {
      const originMaxAge = parseInt(maxAgeMatch[1], 10);

      // Step 6a — Clone the response (origin Response is immutable)
      const response = new Response(originResponse.body, originResponse);

      // Step 6b — Override CDN TTL via s-maxage, preserve browser TTL
      response.headers.set(
        "Cache-Control",
        `public, s-maxage=${CLOUDFLARE_CDN_TTL}, max-age=${originMaxAge}`
      );

      // Step 6c — Store non-blocking (don't delay the response)
      ctx.waitUntil(cache.put(cacheKey, response.clone()));

      return response;
    }

    // Step 6d — No max-age from origin: pass through without caching
    return originResponse;
  },
};

Cache-Control header anatomy

The difference between the browser TTL and the CDN TTL is the whole point.

Cache-Control: public, s-maxage=3600, max-age=300
                       |                    |
                       |                    +- browser TTL: 300s (from origin)
                       +- CDN / Cloudflare edge TTL: 3600s (set by the Worker)
DirectiveControlsWho sets itSeen by browser?
max-ageBrowser / client cache TTLOrigin (preserved by Worker)Yes
s-maxageCDN / proxy TTL (Cloudflare edge)Worker (set to 3600)No — stripped at edge
cf.cacheTtlEdge TTL, ignores origin headersfetch() cf option (before request)No
cf.cacheTtlByStatusEdge TTL per HTTP statusfetch() cf option (before request)No

Why each API call matters

cache.match(cacheKey)

Looks up the request in this data center’s cache. Returns the cached Response or undefined. Check it first to avoid needless origin trips.

new Response(body, init)

Origin responses are immutable — you can’t edit their headers. Cloning into a new Response() gives a mutable copy to rewrite before caching.

cache.put(key, response.clone())

Stores the response. .clone() is mandatory: a body stream is consumed once — one copy goes to the user, the other to the cache.

ctx.waitUntil()

Keeps the Worker alive to finish cache.put() after the response is sent. Without it, the cache write is cancelled when the handler returns.

Decision tree

The Worker’s branching logic on every request.

Request received |-- Method is GET or HEAD? | |-- NO -> fetch(request) and return (pass-through) | +-- YES -> check cache | |-- cache.match() returns a response? | |-- YES -> return cached response (CF-Cache-Status: HIT) | +-- NO -> fetch from origin | |-- originResponse.ok (2xx)? | |-- NO -> return error response (not cached) | +-- YES -> parse Cache-Control | +-- Origin header has max-age=x? |-- NO -> return originResponse (pass-through, not cached) +-- YES -> clone -> set s-maxage=3600 -> cache.put() -> return

CF-Cache-Status header

Cloudflare adds CF-Cache-Status so you can verify behaviour in DevTools or curl -I.

HIT

Served from edge cache. Origin not contacted.

MISS

Not cached. Fetched from origin and stored for next time.

EXPIRED

Was cached but the s-maxage TTL elapsed. Re-fetched.

BYPASS

Cache intentionally skipped (cookie, no-store, etc.).

DYNAMIC

Not cached — no matching rule / CF chose not to.

What to watch out for

No Tiered Cache

caches.default does not propagate through Cloudflare’s Tiered Cache. If you need it, use fetch() with cf.cacheTtl (which requires knowing the TTL up front).

Cache is per data center

The Cache API stores per edge PoP. A request landing on a different PoP is a MISS and re-fetches until that PoP warms up too.

Body consumed once

Always response.clone() before cache.put(), or one of the user / cache copies gets an empty body.

Vary interactions

An origin Vary header (e.g. Accept-Encoding) adds those request headers to the cache key — watch for cache fragmentation.

Deploy it

The source lives in workers/cache-override/. Bind it to this route so the page above is served through it.

# workers/cache-override/wrangler.toml (route)
routes = [
  { pattern = "www.pimenta.fun/cache/cache-worker*", zone_name = "pimenta.fun" }
]

# deploy
cd workers/cache-override
npx wrangler deploy
  • Verify with curl -sI https://www.pimenta.fun/cache/cache-worker/ | grep -i cf-cache-status.
  • First request: MISS; subsequent (same PoP, within the TTL): HIT.
